as well as BW Group and the Group's banking counterparties.</div> <div> </div> <div>You will be responsible for Group cash and liquidity management, credit support, FX and hedging operations, cash investment, banking and treasury facilities, treasury governance and treasury systems.</div> <div> </div> <div>Your objective is to replace fragmented activity with a coherent Group treasury capability: giving management reliable visibility of cash, liquidity and treasury risk, ensuring cash and credit resources are deployed efficiently, strengthening controls and banking infrastructure, and building processes and systems that scale with the business.</div> <div> </div> <div><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>Cash management: own the consolidated Group cash position across corporate entities, project SPVs, joint ventures, accounts and currencies, including restricted and unrestricted cash, intercompany funding, equity contributions and distributions, and ensuring the right cash sits in the right entity, account and currency ahead of material payment obligations.</div> </li> <li> <div>Liquidity management: own the Group liquidity position and rolling forecast, consolidating inputs from Portfolio FP&A, Accounting, Investments, Strategic Finance and project teams, and providing forward-looking analysis of requirements, constraints, surpluses and funding needs across multiple currencies and jurisdictions.</div> </li> <li> <div>Credit support: own the portfolio of bank guarantees, parent-company guarantees, letters of credit and other contingent exposures, managing issuance, amendment, renewal and cancellation, and monitoring utilisation, expiries, fees, collateral and facility headroom.</div> </li> <li> <div>FX management: own the consolidated view of forecast and actual FX exposures across development, construction, operations and corporate activity, maintain the Group's FX framework, recommend hedging actions, and execute approved transactions within delegated authorities.</div> </li> <li> <div>Cash investment: manage surplus cash within approved policies and counterparty limits, optimising deposit arrangements, managing counterparty exposure and diversification, and negotiating terms to improve returns while preserving liquidity.</div> </li> <li> <div>Hedging operations: own the operational management of FX and interest-rate derivatives, including execution, confirmation, settlement, records of hedges and maturities, collateral and threshold monitoring, and treasury inputs into valuation, accounting and reporting.</div> </li> <li> <div>Banking and facilities: act as principal treasury relationship owner for cash-management and transaction banks, maintain the Group's banking architecture (accounts, mandates, signatories, access, KYC and documentation), own treasury-related facilities, and support complex funds flows for acquisitions, disposals, financings, refinancings and project financial close.</div> </li> <li> <div>Controls, policy and governance: own treasury policies, procedures, delegated authorities and the control framework, ensure transactions are authorised, documented, reconciled and auditable, monitor compliance with policy and counterparty limits, and report to senior management and governance forums.</div> </li> <li> <div>Systems and transformation: define the future treasury operating model, lead Treasury's contribution to the Group's ERP implementation, drive automation of cash visibility, forecasting, payments and bank-statement collection, and assess the role and timing of a dedicated Treasury Management System.</div> </li> </ul> <div><strong>Required Skills and Experience</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>10+ years' relevant experience in corporate treasury, infrastructure, energy, banking or a closely related finance role.</div> </li> <li> <div>Demonstrable experience taking ownership of treasury activities in a complex, multi-entity, multi-currency organisation.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong practical experience across cash and liquidity management, FX, banking, credit support and treasury controls.</div> </li> <li> <div>Experience managing senior relationships with banks and other financial counterparties.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong understanding of treasury risk management, with the ability to translate financial exposures into practical recommendations and actions.</div> </li> <li> <div>Ability to operate effectively across multiple legal entities, jurisdictions, currencies and stakeholders.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong judgement and the confidence to identify issues, challenge existing practice and recommend solutions to senior management.</div> </li> <li> <div>Comfortable working hands-on while building more scalable processes, controls and systems.</div> </li> <li> <div>Strong analytical capability and the ability to communicate complex treasury issues clearly and concisely.</div> </li> <li> <div>ACT, ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent professional qualification preferred.</div> </li> </ul> <div><strong>Preferred Experience</strong></div> <ul> <li> <div>Energy, renewables, infrastructure, utilities or another project- and SPV-based business.</div> </li> <li> <div>Treasury within a business undergoing rapid international growth.</div> </li> <li> <div>Project finance, including restricted cash, reserve accounts and project-level funding structures.</div> </li> <li> <div>Bank guarantees, letters of credit, parent-company guarantees and other project credit support.</div> operational support, production debugging and incident response for the BI stack, and fix the root causes you find</p> </li> <li> <p>Champion engineering standards in BI, including version control, code review, CI and testing for models and platform code, so changes ship safely and repeatably</p> </li> </ul> <h2><strong>We’re excited about you because…</strong></h2> <ul> <li> <p>3+ years of experience in business intelligence engineering, analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar code-first data role</p> </li> <li> <p>Strong Python and SQL skills, and hands-on experience using AI tools (LLMs, agentic workflows, AI-assisted development) to accelerate your own engineering work</p> </li> <li> <p>Hands-on experience building in a BI platform such as Looker (LookML) or Sigma, modelling and configuring it, not only building dashboards in it</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience with semantic or metrics layers (LookML, dbt or similar): defining metrics and dimensions, and keeping those definitions consistent as they are reused</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience running what you build in production: version control, code review, CI, debugging live issues and taking part in operational support</p> </li> <li> <p>Excellent communication skills, and comfortable self-organising in a fast-paced, distributed environment with both technical and non-technical teams</p> </li> <p>Experience automating BI administration through platform APIs, or identity and access through Okta, SCIM or role-based access controls</p> </li> <li> <p>Experience supporting a BI stack across title: Senior Sales Manager - Issuing
description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The Role Checkout.com are actively looking for an enthusiastic and talented Senior Sales Manager to join our Commercial Team in London to drive rapid growth for our revolutionary Card Issuing solution. We need a high-achieving individual to help global enterprises launch modern card programs—from virtual cards for travel intermediaries to physical cards for BNPL. If you are a driven and focused salesperson with a proven track record of selling cutting edge issuing solutions in a high-growth and competitive environment, this is the role for you. In return, on top of a tremendous working environment, we offer you an unrivalled uncapped recurring commissions plan. Reporting to the Director, the Senior Sales Manager will handle multiple sales cycles, always ensuring a high conversion rate and outperforming the sales targets. Along the way, you'll collaborate closely with various in-house talents across Technology and Business to position our capabilities, products, services and solutions effectively with prospects. The ideal candidate will need to be an independent, high-achieving individual, able to stand out in an entrepreneurial environment and outperform sales targets through personal drive. How You’ll Make an Impact Pipeline Growth: Identify the most promising clients and grow a healthy pipeline for card issuing across various verticals. Solution Selling: Sell our issuing products to travel intermediaries and fintech clients through outbound techniques. Consultative Expert: Help prospects evaluate Checkout.com, handling detailed questions about our product capabilities, serving as a consultant and industry expert. Proposal Management: Prepare thorough presentations and proposals that highlight the ROI of switching to a modern issuer. Full Cycle Orchestration: Lead the entire Sales process, acting as the main point of contact for clients and internal stakeholders. Collaboration: Partner with other Sales team members to share best practices, key business insights and industry trends Market Intelligence: Provide feedback on local trends including competitor insights, customer needs, sales, product and marketing information What We’re Looking For Experience: 5+ years of Sales experience, with at least 3 years specifically within Payments or Card Issuing. Network: A solid network of potential prospects and partners. AI & Productivity: Proficient in leveraging AI-powered sales tools to augment prospecting and analyze deal intelligence to accelerate the sales cycle. Technical Passion: Tech-savvy with a passion for how technology is transforming finance. title: Director of Quality
description: About LILT AI is changing how the world communicates — and LILT is leading that transformation. We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. We use cutting-edge AI, machine translation, and human-in-the-loop expertise to translate content faster, more accurately, and more cost-effectively without compromising on brand, voice, or quality. At LILT, we empower our teammates with leading tools, global collaboration, and growth opportunities to do their best work. Our company virtues— Work together, win together; Find a way or make one; Dance in the customer's shoes; Quicker than they expect; Quality is Job 1 —guide everything we do. We are trusted by Intel Corporation , Canva , the United States Department of Defense , the United States Air Force , ASICS , and hundreds of global Enterprises. Backed by Sequoia, Intel Capital, and Redpoint, we’re building a category-defining company in a $50B+ global translation market being redefined by AI. Location: Remote or hybrid, EMEA or US Eastern time zone Team: Production, Quality Reports to: VP Production Direct reports: Quality Manager (AMER, customer staffing) and 2 Quality Coordinators About the role As Director of Quality, you will own LILT's quality system end to end: standards, audit, compliance, procedures, continuous improvement, and the roadmap and operation of our Quality Agents . You'll help move Quality from a primarily reactive, execution-led function to a proactive, data-driven partner for customers and internal teams, with quality designed into our AI-native workflows. You'll be the person who can run a customer audit while simultaneously shipping an improved agent evaluation. As the single Quality partner for Customer Success, Production, Research and Product, you'll turn customer requirements into measurable acceptance criteria, effective controls and better models and workflows. You'll advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix, including where automated, agent-verified and human-verified workflows are appropriate, with stronger assurance for high-risk and regulated content. We're looking for a hands-on Quality SME and operator with real depth in both worlds: experience designing and building AI agents and improving LLM output, and a solid grounding in traditional quality management. You'll bring senior expertise in data, AI, customer advisory and process, and make sure quality work prevents recurrence rather than stopping at rework or ticket closure. What you'll do Quality Agent leadership Evaluate, design and build reliable Quality Agents with well-defined tools and clear, structured instructions. Use orchestration patterns to evolve from a single agent to multi-agent systems. Define evaluation criteria, test sets and success metrics for agent performance, and run agents in production with clear monitoring and escalation paths. Drive adoption across teams and show measurable reductions in manual quality effort. Research and Product partnership Work closely with Research and Product on ADQ, LLM model improvements, AI Review, AI QA, and new and emerging AI workflows. Turn quality findings into product requirements, evaluation criteria and continuous feedback loops that improve model and workflow output. Act as the voice of quality in roadmap discussions, and help decide where human review, AI review or both are needed. Audit, compliance and procedure Own LILT's approach to internal and external audits, including ISO certification (e.g. ISO 17100, ISO 18587, ISO 9001) and customer audits. Plan and run periodic internal audits, manage evidence collection, and track corrective and preventive actions to closure. Standardise and maintain SOPs, workflows and quality documentation, and keep them current as AI workflows change how we work. Make sure quality processes meet customer, contractual and regulatory requirements. Customer advisory Partner with Customer Success and Delivery to define proactive quality programmes, success metrics and governance for strategic accounts, including AI-forward enterprise and life science / regulatory programmes. Translate customer quality requirements into clear pre-delivery acceptance criteria, validation methods and risk-appropriate controls. Advise customers on the right quality, cost and speed mix and where automated, agent-verified, human-verified or combined workflows are appropriate. Represent LILT's quality function as a credible subject-matter authority in customer business reviews, audits and escalations, using quality data and metrics to demonstrate fitness for purpose. Continuous improvement Lead structured CI across the Commercial business: root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, KPI reviews and retrospectives. Own a proactive quality metrics framework that makes errors, PQs, rework and trends visible, and use it to prioritise improvements and demonstrate outcomes. Strengthen quality controls across review, delivery and follow-through, including mandatory account-specific checks, intervention on critical findings and clear escalation ownership. Partner with Product and Engineering to automate checks and escalation, and verify that corrective actions prevent recurrence rather than ending at rework or ticket closure. Expert Operations partnership Partner with Expert Supply and Ops to embed processes, guidance and quality feedback that maintain a high-quality pipeline of experts. Use quality findings and recurring failure patterns to improve expert qualification, guidance and ongoing quality management. Team leadership Lead and develop the Quality team, including the customer-facing Quality Manager and Quality Coordinators. Establish the team's operating cadence and evolve how the team works as Quality Agents reduce manual coordination work. Oversee embedded Quality Manager staffing sold as a service to customers, ensuring the role owns the specific quality programmes and initiatives those customers pay for. Develop playbooks for AI-driven quality management and keep staffing-as-a-service delivery aligned with LILT's quality standards. What you'll bring Must have Agent design and build: demonstrable, hands-on experience designing, building and running LLM-based agents in production. Please be ready to walk us through agents you have built. Data-driven quality management: scripting or data skills (e.g. Python, SQL), with experience turning quality data into actionable metrics, preventive controls and measurable improvements. LLM model improvement: proven experience improving LLM output quality. Significant experience running quality systems , including leading audits (internal and external), compliance programmes, and writing and maintaining processes and procedures. Quality certifications such as Six Sigma are a plus. Experience leading structured CI (RCA, CAPA, KPI reviews). Experience managing and developing people. Customer advisory and cross-functional partnership: a clear communicator who can translate customer quality requirements into acceptance criteria and governance, advise on quality, cost and speed trade-offs, and work credibly with customers, executives and technical teams. Nice to have Background in localisation, translation or language services. Experience in customer-facing quality roles for enterprise accounts. Research and Product collaboration: a track record of working with research scientists and product managers to turn quality insight into product requirements and shipped improvements. Our Story Our founders, Spence and John met at Google working on Google Translate. As researchers at Stanford and Berkeley, they both worked on language technology to make information accessible to everyone. While together at Google, they were amazed to learn that Google Translate wasn’t used for enterprise products and services inside the company.The quality just wasn’t there. So they set out to build something better. LILT was born. LILT has been a machine learning company since its founding in 2015. At the time, machine translation didn’t meet the quality standard for enterprise translations, so LILT assembled a cutting-edge research team tasked with closing that gap. While meeting customer demand for translation services, LILT has prioritized investments in Large Language Models, human-in-the-loop systems, and now agentic AI. With AI innovation accelerating and enterprise demand growing, the next phase of LILT’s journey is just beginning. Our Tech What sets our platform apart: Brand-aware AI that learns your voice, tone, and terminology to ensure every translation is accurate and consistent Agentic AI workflows that automate the entire translation process from content ingestion to quality review to publishing 100+ native integrations with systems like Adobe Experience Manager, Webflow, Salesforce, GitHub, and Google Drive to simplify content translation Human-in-the-loop reviews via our global network of professional linguists, for high-impact content that requires expert review LILT in the News Featured in The Software Report’s Top 100 Software Companies! LILT makes it onto the Inc. 5000 List . LILT’s continues to be an intellectual powerhouse, holding numerous patents that help power the most efficient and sophisticated AI and language models in the industry. title: Retail Industry Principal
description: About SINGU At SINGU , we’re redefining how the world’s most ambitious real estate companies run their operations. Our mission is to become Europe’s leading platform for managing warehouse, logistics, retail, and multi-site commercial real estate portfolios — empowering our Clients to protect revenue, boost efficiency, and unlock new value across every aspect of their business. Our unified CAFM platform already powers the daily operations of over 250 million m² of real estate worldwide , supporting more than 500,000 professionals. Following our union with the UK’s Micad and Germany’s net-haus, we now help manage 100,000+ buildings across 35+ countries — and we’re just getting started. Backed by a leading growth equity investor, we’re scaling rapidly and partnering with global leaders such as Prologis, ECE, CTP, Hillwood, Logicor, GLP, and Unibail-Rodamco-Westfield. As we continue to grow through strategic acquisitions and bold innovation, we stay true to our core values: adaptability, collaboration, and client focus. If you’re ready to help build Europe’s leading platform for property operations — and make a tangible impact on how the real estate industry works — join SINGU and be part of this transformation. The Opportunity SINGU provides property and facilities management technology for organisations operating complex, multi-site estates . Retail is a strategically important market for the business, spanning shopping centres, retail parks, high-street portfolios, supermarkets, hospitality and other distributed consumer environments. We are seeking an experienced retail property, facilities or operations leader to become SINGU's senior market authority for retail and help build a differentiated, commercially successful position in the sector. The Retail Market Principal will combine deep industry expertise, executive credibility and market leadership with clear commercial accountability . The role will help SINGU determine where it has the strongest right to win , create access to senior decision-makers , originate strategic opportunities , accelerate priority deals and strengthen SINGU's relevance across the retail property and facilities ecosystem. This is not a conventional sales, pre-sales, product marketing or communications role . It is a senior, market-facing position for someone who understands retail property and operations at practitioner level and can translate that experience, credibility and network into measurable commercial impact . Success will be measured not simply through market visibility or activity, but through SINGU's ability to create qualified pipeline , win strategic customers , expand existing relationships and establish a repeatable position within priority retail segments . What Success Looks Like Within the first 12 months , you will have established a clear and credible retail go-to-market strategy , identifying the segments and use cases where SINGU can win disproportionately and building meaningful executive relationships across priority retail accounts . You will have originated and influenced significant qualified pipeline , contributed demonstrably to both new-logo and expansion revenue , and developed repeatable retail propositions supported by clear customer evidence . You will also have strengthened SINGU's network of retail customers and advocates , while materially increasing our credibility, relevance and market position within the retail property and facilities sector. What You Will Own Retail Market Strategy: Define where SINGU has the strongest right to win across retail. Shape our retail go-to-market strategy , priority segments, use cases and target accounts . Maintain a strong point of view on the operational, regulatory and technology issues shaping retail estates. Translate market insight into clear commercial and product priorities . Executive Access and Market Development: Build trusted relationships with senior leaders across retail property, facilities, operations, asset management and transformation. Use your network and industry credibility to create access to strategic prospects and originate new opportunities . Represent SINGU in executive forums , customer meetings, roundtables and selected industry events . Build relationships across the wider retail ecosystem , including advisers, FM providers, managing agents and partners. Strategic Accounts and Commercial Impact: Work with Sales and Customer Success on a focused portfolio of priority retail accounts . Help uncover strategic priorities, strengthen business cases and improve executive engagement . Support selected opportunities where your involvement can materially increase SINGU's probability of winning . Identify expansion opportunities across customers, countries, sites, modules and use cases. Contribute directly to qualified pipeline and revenue growth , without replacing the accountable salesperson . Customer and Market Insight: Build a strong community of retail customers, advocates and industry influencers . Bring structured market insight into Product, Product Marketing and Commercial Strategy. Identify repeatable customer needs , emerging opportunities and gaps in SINGU's proposition. Help ensure SINGU invests in problems that customers are willing to pay to solve . Commercial Accountability: This is not a conventional quota-carrying role , but it has clear commercial accountability . Performance will be measured against: qualified pipeline originated and materially influenced; revenue contribution from strategic retail opportunities; progression and penetration of priority accounts; executive relationships created within target organisations; development of repeatable retail propositions and use cases ; customer advocacy and market influence . Specific commercial targets will be agreed annually . What We're Looking For: Significant senior experience in retail property, facilities management, estates, operations or asset management. First-hand understanding of complex, multi-site retail estates . Strong credibility and an established network with senior retail stakeholders . Evidence of turning industry relationships and insight into commercial opportunities or strategic outcomes. Strong commercial judgement and the ability to connect operational challenges to financial value, risk and business outcomes . Executive presence , strong communication skills and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively . The ability to identify what is genuinely scalable and commercially valuable , rather than simply interesting. Experience in software or technology is helpful but not essential ; deep retail credibility and commercial instinct matter more. Business-fluent English ; Polish and/or German language is an advantage Package and Progression: Competitive base salary , calibrated to experience and location. Performance-related bonus linked to strategic-account engagement, market influence and measurable commercial contribution. Direct sponsorship from the CRO and access to SINGU's executive leadership . Support from Sales, Marketing, Product Marketing, Product and Pre-Sales . The opportunity to shape SINGU's retail market position across Europe . Progression into broader market leadership , strategic growth or industry-led go-to-market responsibility. If this role sounds like a good fit, we’d love to hear from you. title: Strategic Account Manager

In this role, you will act as the primary point of contact for our largest hospitality customers across the UK region. You will be responsible for driving growth, product adoption, and stakeholder management within your portfolio, with the goal of building true business partnerships. You will leverage data, customer feedback, and your SaaS expertise to create value at the enterprise level. Lightspeed is a proud equal opportunity employer and we are committed to creating an inclusive and barrier-free workplace. Lightspeed welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in all aspects of the selection process. Where to from here? Obviously, this has to be mutually beneficial: we want you to step into a role you love, and we want to offer you a place you’re proud to come to every day. For a glimpse into our world check out our career page here . Lightspeed is building communities through commerce, and we need people from all backgrounds and lived experiences to do that. We were founded in 2005, in Montreal’s gay village and our original members were all part of the LGBTQ+ community. The ethos of our business has been about inclusion from the very beginning, and we strive to provide a workplace where everyone belongs. Who we are: Powering the businesses that are the backbone of the global economy, Lightspeed's one-stop commerce platform helps merchants innovate to simplify, scale, and provide exceptional customer experiences. Our cloud commerce solution transforms and unifies online and physical operations, multichannel sales, expansion to new locations, global payments, financial solutions, and connection to supplier networks. Founded in Montréal, Canada in 2005, Lightspeed is dual-listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: LSPD) and Toronto Stock Exchange (TSX: LSPD). With teams across North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, the company serves retail, hospitality, and golf businesses in over 100 countries. description: Could you be the person we are looking for to join us as our new Senior People Advisor - MATS in Grangemouth? We want to hear from you. About the Role We are currently looking for an experienced and commercially minded Senior People Advisor to join us, acting as the dedicated HR lead for our Marine and Terminal Services (MATS) business area. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced HR professional who enjoys working closely with operational leaders, managing complex employee relations matters, supporting organisational change and helping to build management capability. As Senior People Advisor – MATS, you will be the primary HR contact for managers and employees across the division, providing expert advice and practical support across all aspects of the employee lifecycle. You will lead on complex employee relations matters, support workforce planning and organisational change, build strong relationships with managers, and help develop leadership capability across the business. This role offers the opportunity to make a real impact by influencing people decisions, supporting business performance and contributing to the continued development of GAC's people strategy. What would your day at GAC look like? Act as the dedicated HR lead for Marine & Terminal Services (MATS), building strong relationships with managers and employees and providing commercially focused HR support. Partner with managers to support workforce planning, recruitment, succession planning and organisational change initiatives. Support workforce transitions and TUPE related activity Lead and manage employee relations matters including disciplinary, grievance, absence, capability and performance processes. Build and maintain positive relationships with trade union representatives and support consultation and industrial relations activities. Coach and develop managers to improve capability, consistency and confidence in managing people matters. Support employee engagement, wellbeing and culture initiatives that contribute to retention and organisational performance. Identify skills gaps and development needs within the business and support learning, leadership and career development initiatives. Use people data and insights to identify trends, risks and opportunities and support effective decision-making. Support the Head of People in delivering the HR strategy, driving continuous improvement and developing management capability across the business. Mentor and support the development of junior members of the HR team, helping to build future capability within the function. What are we looking for? We are looking for someone who brings both strong employee relations expertise and the ability to build trusted relationships with operational managers. You will ideally have: CIPD Level 5 qualification (or equivalent experience). Significant experience in a generalist HR or HR Advisory role. Strong experience managing complex employee relations matters. Experience working with trade unions Sound knowledge of UK and Irish employment legislation. Experience supporting managers in operational environments. Experience in supporting TUPE transfers Excellent communication, coaching and influencing skills. The ability to work independently whilst collaborating effectively with colleagues and stakeholders. A proactive, organised and commercially focused approach to HR. What’s in it for you? This is your chance to become part of the global GAC team which has been providing professional shipping, logistics and marine services since 1956. Everything we do is guided by the GAC Spirit, built on mutual loyalty between management and staff, and a belief in the value of our people as individuals - not just for the jobs they do. With more than 7,500 colleagues in 300 strategically located offices in more than 50 countries around the world, we focus on quality, safety and sustainability with a human touch. Emphasising a long-term approach, innovation and ethics, our flexible and integrated portfolios are designed to work within and support our customers’ operations. As our Senior People Advisor - MATS in Grangemouth you will have the opportunity to work as part of a team who apply the highest standard of customer services to everything we do and aim to be industry leaders within all the sectors we serve. GAC UK gives you the opportunity to work for an employer who is committed to offering all our staff an enjoyable and rewarding career, with significant training and development prospects. Throughout the year, we will be raising funds to support CALM’s life‑saving suicide prevention helpline. We’re looking forward to hearing from you. title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, ADAS
description: Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve. We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that. Here’s what this particular role covers. 🛠️ About our ADAS Team Wayve's ADAS engineering teams build the perception and intelligence that power driver assistance in real-world driving. We work end-to-end, from creating high-quality training data, to developing and evaluating CV/3D perception models, to iterating quickly based on performance gaps. The team mixes "online" (on-car, latency/compute constrained) and "offline" (heavier, large-scale data generation) work, with a strong focus on measurable impact and shipping. 🧠 Your day-to-day Train, debug, and improve computer vision and 3D perception models, iterating based on clear evaluation signals Work across the full ML lifecycle: data, training, evaluation, and iteration Partner with the team to decide what to tackle next, based on where the system is underperforming Build scalable data pipelines, including auto-labelling and pseudo-labelling, to accelerate model development 🧩 What you'll be working on: Core ADAS perception capabilities such as detection, classification, and instance segmentation, spanning lanes, objects, traffic signs, and traffic lights End-to-end approaches that let the model act on the world directly, rather than relying on a chain of hand-coded intermediate steps (lane assist without ever explicitly detecting lane lines is the kind of outcome we're after) Online perception that runs fast in-car as part of our production stack Offline perception work using additional inputs not viable for on-road production, including extra sensors like lidar, future frames, maps, and extra compute, to improve data quality and coverage at scale Building the "data flywheel": using offline models and 3D tracking/reconstruction to auto-generate labels and accelerate iteration across perception tasks 👤 You should apply if: Built and shipped CV-focused deep learning systems, with strong applied ML engineering rather than research-only work Experience Enjoy pragmatic problem-solving under real product constraints Excited to improve real-world driving performance through better perception Automotive domain experience is a bonus, but not a blocker if your perception background comes from elsewhere 🌱 Not ticking every box? That's totally okay! If you're passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don't meet every requirement. More about Wayve: 🚗 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines. Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve's mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility. How we work 💻 — Locations & Flexible Working: Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives. 📋 The Interview Process: Our process is clear and respectful of your time: Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins) Competency interviews (programming and system design; 2 hours) Deep-dive technical interviews (Hiring manager/Domain Interview; 1 hour) Final interview : mission & values alignment (1 hour) We'll always explain the format and work around your availability. Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one. If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you. title: Senior People Partner
description: Senior People Partner Cloudscaler | London | People Team | Reports to the Chief People Officer | £55,000–£75,000 Someone has to own the People initiative that doesn’t fit neatly into anyone’s week and the case nobody else should be handling. That someone is you — not as an escalation point, but as the person who runs the day-to-day of this function. THE MOMENT Cloudscaler is 130 people today. We’ll be 170 by the end of this year, and roughly double again in 2027. The People function is being built in real time alongside that growth, rather than inherited from someone who left years ago. You’ll be the first hire into the People team. For roughly your first year you’ll be the only People professional alongside the CPO, which means running the whole day-to-day of the function: the hardest casework and initiatives, and the operational core that keeps everything moving. A People Partner is planned to join later in 2027, and at that point the operational administration moves to them. This is also a role built with room to grow. As the team expands beyond that second hire, we expect this role to take on day-to-day operational leadership of the People Partner practice, but that isn’t the shape of it on day one. WHAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT In most People teams, the senior generalist is just a People Partner with a harder case queue. Here, the difference is ownership, not just difficulty. Complex casework: Rather than simply handling harder cases, you’ll own the most complex cases end to end, with no hand back. People initiatives: Rather than contributing to initiatives someone else drives, you’ll own them from design through to embedding. Decision-making: Rather than escalating ambiguity upward, you’ll make the sensible call and document your reasoning. CPO partnership: Rather than acting in a support role to the CPO, you’ll be an operational partner they can confidently delegate to. To be clear about the level: The CPO still designs the People strategy and the systems architecture. You own how it runs day to day, and you’re trusted to run a whole initiative, not just a case. That is a different job to People Partner, not a bigger version of the same one. THE ROLE You’ll sit in the People team reporting to the Chief People Officer. Three strands make up the job: Casework: The employee relations situations with the most complexity or sensitivity land with you, start to finish. Initiatives: When the CPO needs a piece of work owned (a policy rollout, a wellbeing programme, a piece of the reward or benefits agenda), you take it from design through to something that runs. Operations: Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own payroll and benefits administration, onboarding, screening and security clearances, and keeping Rippling accurate. When the People Partner joins, they’ll report to the CPO. You won’t manage them formally, but you’ll lead their handover, you’ll be the person they come to first, and your judgement will set the standard for how this function operates day to day. WHERE THE ROLE STARTS AND STOPS New roles get vague, so here is the boundary as we see it today. Yours The most complex and sensitive employee relations casework, end to end. Full ownership of People initiatives, from design to embedding. Acting as the CPO’s operational partner on ambiguous or cross-cutting problems. Until the People Partner joins (planned for later in 2027): Payroll and benefits administration, including the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling and Mintago. Pre-onboarding, onboarding and probation. Background screening in Zinc. Security clearance coordination. Rippling data quality, workflows and reporting. Our working groups and committees. Once the People Partner joins: A structured handover of the operational core. Day-to-day guidance for the People Partner. Shared Ashby, which Talent Acquisition owns. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on every hire until the People Partner joins, and on senior hires after that. Mentoring and supporting the People Partner on their casework and initiatives, once they join. Not yours Recruitment delivery, which sits with Talent Acquisition. The design of the People strategy, the operating model and the systems architecture, which sit with the CPO. Formal line management of the People Partner, who will report to the CPO. THE STACK Rippling: Our single source of truth. Until the People Partner joins you’ll run it day to day, including the monthly payroll cycle, data quality and workflows, and you’ll use its reporting at a level that supports whole initiatives. Zinc: Background screening. You’ll run checks for every new joiner until the People Partner joins, and stay close to the senior and sensitive hires after that. Ashby: Owned by Talent Acquisition. You’ll work in it from offer through to start date on the hires you’re responsible for. Claude: A daily tool here. You’ll use it for casework preparation, drafting policy and communications, and pulling together the analysis behind an initiative. Mintago: Our employee benefits and financial wellbeing platform (pensions, salary sacrifice and financial advice). You’ll administer it and keep enrolment accurate until the People Partner takes it on. WHAT YOU’LL DO Own the hardest casework. You’ll run our most complex and sensitive employee relations cases end to end, with the CPO there to sense-check rather than take over. Own initiatives, not tasks. You’ll take a People initiative from a rough brief to something that’s running and embedded, rather than handing it back once the interesting part is done. Run the operational core. Until the People Partner joins, you’ll own the monthly payroll cycle in Rippling, benefits administration including Mintago, onboarding, background screening and security clearances. Accurate, on time, and documented as you go. Hand it over well. When the People Partner arrives, you’ll give them a working system and a clear handover, then stay the person they come to first and the judgement others in the function measure themselves against. Partner with senior leaders. You’ll be credible with leaders on the most difficult conversations: complex change, capability, and situations without a clean playbook. Use AI properly. You’ll use Claude daily to take time out of your own week, checking anything that touches a decision about a person and owning the outcome. Improve what you find. You’ll spot the gaps in policy, process or practice before anyone else does, and bring the CPO a considered view on the fix, not just the problem. WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT 12 MONTHS You’re running the most complex ER cases with confidence, and the CPO isn’t being pulled into them. At least one or two People initiatives have gone from a rough brief to something genuinely embedded, owned by you. Payroll, benefits, onboarding and clearances run accurately and on time, and every process is documented well enough to hand over. You’ve helped shape the People Partner hire, so the handover is ready when they land. Senior leaders treat you as a credible operational partner, not an escalation point. You’ve made and documented sensible calls in genuinely ambiguous situations, and they’ve held up. The CPO can hand you an ambiguous problem and trust it gets shaped properly. WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR Deep employee relations experience. You’ve run complex disciplinaries, grievances and change situations yourself, and you know exactly when to escalate and when not to. CIPD qualification, or solid progress towards it, is welcome. A track record of owning initiatives. You can point to work you took from a brief to something that actually ran, not just a project you contributed to. Hands-on with the operational detail. You’ve owned or closely supported a payroll cycle, benefits administration and onboarding, and you’re comfortable being accountable for their accuracy while also carrying the senior work. Credible with senior leaders. You can hold your own in a difficult conversation with someone under real pressure and be listened to. Comfortable operating near-autonomously. You don’t need a playbook for everything. You make a sensible call, write it down, and check it with the CPO afterwards. Ready to grow into people leadership. You won’t formally manage anyone at the start, but you’ll induct and guide the People Partner when they join, and you should want to lead a team as the structure catches up. Discreet and organised at volume. Complex casework and live initiatives, often at the same time. You’ll need a system, and it can’t be your memory. THE HONEST PART This role sits in an odd space for now: senior in scope and judgement, without a team underneath it yet. Until the People Partner joins later in 2027, you’ll also be the whole operational team, so a payroll deadline and a complex grievance can land in the same week. That eases as the function grows, but it means the authority you carry day to day has to come from the quality of your work, not a job title. You are not designing the People strategy or the systems architecture. The CPO does that. What you get instead is real ownership of the hardest cases and the initiatives that matter, a close working relationship with the CPO, and a genuine path toward leading the People Partner practice as it grows. This probably isn’t for you if you want a formal team from day one, or if you’d rather leave payroll and onboarding to someone else. It probably is for you if you want to prove you can run this function well enough, top to bottom, that a team gets built around you. If that sounds like the challenge you’ve been looking for, let’s talk. title: Senior Manager, Credit Risk
description: About Airwallex Airwallex is the AI-native financial operating system for a real-time, intelligent economy. More than 675,000 businesses, including McLaren Racing, Qantas, SHEIN, and TikTok, use us, directly or through our platform partners, to run their financial operations or build and monetize financial products of their own. We started in Melbourne in 2015 to build the infrastructure global commerce runs on. We're the regulated backbone behind global payments: not by accident, but by design. A decade plus, 85+ licenses, and a financial infrastructure spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific. We're co-headquartered in San Francisco and Singapore, with more than 2,300 people across 27 offices. We hire builders with founder-level energy, people who move fast with good judgment, dig in with real curiosity, and make calls from first principles rather than waiting to be told what to do. Read our operating principles to see it in full. About the team The Credit Risk team is part of Airwallex’s Second Line of Defence and helps the company grow responsibly as a global financial platform. We work at the intersection of credit, FX, and counterparty risk, partnering closely with Product, Sales, Operations, Treasury, Finance, Engineering, Compliance, and Legal to enable commercial growth while protecting Airwallex from financial loss and excessive risk exposure. This is a team for analytical, commercially minded risk leaders who are energized by building scalable frameworks and practical controls across a fast-moving, multi-currency global network. What you'll do As a Senior Manager, Credit Risk, you will lead Airwallex's global second-line oversight of credit, FX, and counterparty risk. You will set the risk guardrails that allow the business to grow safely across merchant acquiring, charge cards, FX, treasury, settlement, and banking-partner activities. Reporting to the Senior Director, Financial Risk, you will own the global framework, risk appetite, limits, governance, and portfolio oversight for these risk areas. You will provide independent challenge to first-line decisions and act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders across the business. This role is based in London. Responsibilities Credit risk framework and risk appetite: Define, implement, and continuously enhance the global second-line credit risk framework, including policies, risk appetite thresholds, limits, escalation protocols, and governance standards across Airwallex’s products and legal entities. Credit portfolio oversight: Oversee credit exposures across merchant acquiring, charge cards, B2B and commercial activities, FX pre-funding, treasury-related exposures, settlement flows, and other relevant products. Underwriting and limit governance: Review and challenge first-line underwriting strategies, customer and merchant risk policies, credit assessments, limit-setting methodologies, and exception processes. Act as a senior escalation point for complex or high-value credit decisions. FX risk oversight: Establish and monitor appropriate second-line guardrails for FX exposures arising from pre-funding, settlement, customer activity, treasury flows, and other multi-currency activities. Challenge controls, limits, escalation triggers, and risk reporting to ensure exposures remain within approved tolerances. Counterparty risk management: Set and oversee counterparty risk standards for banking partners, payment partners, merchants, customers, and other material counterparties. Establish appropriate exposure limits, concentration thresholds, monitoring requirements, and escalation processes. Portfolio monitoring and early warning indicators: Lead proactive monitoring of credit, FX, and counterparty portfolios, including exposure, concentration, delinquency, default, chargeback, loss, settlement, liquidity-of-counterparty, and other relevant risk indicators. Identify emerging trends and escalate material issues before they become systemic. Loss mitigation and remediation: Review and challenge first-line monitoring, collections, collateral, prefunding, reserves, chargeback, and other mitigation strategies. Ensure deteriorating counterparties, customers, merchants, or exposures are identified and addressed promptly. New products and market expansion: Partner with Product, Engineering, Commercial, Treasury, Finance, and Operations to assess and challenge the risk design of new products, features, markets, currencies, and partner arrangements before launch. Risk approvals and governance: Lead or support risk committee decisions, material risk approvals, limit exceptions, breach assessments, and remediation plans. Ensure decisions are documented clearly and aligned with approved risk appetite. Regulatory and partner engagement: Represent Credit Risk during regulatory examinations, internal and external audits, and reviews with banking and strategic partners. Prepare clear, decision-useful materials for senior management, risk committees, and the Board where appropriate. Who you are We're looking for people who meet the minimum requirements for this role. The preferred qualifications are great to have, but are not mandatory. Minimum qualifications 10–15 years of progressively senior experience across credit risk, counterparty risk, FX risk, treasury risk, or related financial risk disciplines within banking, payments, fintech, or another highly regulated financial services environment. Deep experience designing, implementing, and governing second-line credit risk frameworks in a complex, multi-jurisdictional organization. Strong understanding of credit risk identification, measurement, underwriting, limit management, monitoring, mitigation, provisioning, loss recognition, and capital implications. Demonstrated experience managing risk across multiple product lines, such as merchant acquiring, commercial or charge cards, B2B lending, payment processing, FX, treasury, settlement, or banking-partner activities. Practical experience overseeing FX and counterparty risk, including exposure measurement, concentration risk, limits, settlement risk, prefunding, collateral or other mitigants, and escalation governance. Proven ability to challenge first-line decisions and communicate clear risk positions to senior executives, commercial leaders, product and operations teams, banking partners, auditors, and regulators. Preferred qualifications Advanced degree such as an MBA or Master's in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or a related field. Professional certification such as FRM, PRM, CFA, or an equivalent qualification. Experience with automated decisioning engines, credit scoring models, portfolio analytics, or alternative data used in underwriting and monitoring. Familiarity with IFRS 9, expected credit loss methodologies, stress testing, or other relevant prudential and accounting frameworks. Strong data literacy and familiarity with SQL, Python, or similar tools used to analyze portfolio, exposure, and loss trends. Experience working in a regulated payments fintech, digital bank, or financial institution with multiple licenses and banking partnerships. Comfort operating in a high-growth environment with evolving priorities and a bias for practical, scalable execution. title: Head of Data & Intelligence
description: Creandum's edge has always been people: the network, the judgment, the hustle. To sharpen our edge, we need to make everything those people learn compound: every meeting, every diligence process, every founder relationship feeding a shared foundation instead of evaporating into inboxes and individual heads. You will build and own that foundation: the firm's data platform, the intelligence layer on top of it, and the governance that makes partners willing to trust it with their most sensitive work. This is a new function, and you are its first hire. You'll start hands-on-keyboard and stay that way for the time being; but you're building an estate the firm will run on, and the mandate grows with what you prove. You report to the Operating Partner, but work directly and independently with every member of the firm. We believe different viewpoints drive our growth, and we welcome applicants from all backgrounds. What you'll own The data platform. The firm's data architecture end to end: warehouse, ingestion from core systems (CRM, meeting transcripts, documents, email/calendar), entity resolution, and data quality. One person, one company, one deal – consistent across every source. This is foundational; everything else flows from it. The intelligence layer. Retrieval, search & agent tooling that give everyone's AI real firm context, serving both individual workflows (bottom-up) and firm-wide platforms (top-down). Built for passive compounding: the system gets better as people work and as models improve, without depending on anyone's discipline. Access, trust, and AI risk. The access model as structural enforcement, not instructions: who sees what, with identity, provenance, and audit. Sensitive fund and partner data protected to a standard the partnership will trust, plus the AI-specific risk judgment (injection containment, egress, tool guardrails) for everything the function ships, in collaboration with legal/regulatory counsel. Technology strategy and the tool estate. Accountability for whether the firm's tools are the right ones: evaluation, integration, and replacement of the systems and data sources the firm runs on, in close partnership with the stakeholders who use them. Buy when buying is better; build when building is better. You have the mandate to choose, and then execute on your decision. Make sure security, compliance and budget are part of the equation. What you'll deliver First 6 months. A complete map of the firm's data and systems. The foundational data platform stood up. Two or three lightweight tools shipped that visibly improve how a team works. A clear, prioritized 12–18 month roadmap, authored by you and agreed with the partnership. By 12 months. V1 of the firm's shared intelligence layer live and in daily use. The diligence process made genuinely multiplayer; firm knowledge and meeting history informing live deals instead of sitting unused. Measurable adoption, reported honestly, with failures killed as quickly as the wins are shipped. Beyond. The roadmap is yours to define. Candidates for the frontier: productizing how the firm wins deals, network intelligence that answers "who do we know" in seconds, platform tools founders can self-serve, and operational automation across finance, events, and admin. How you'll work Builder first. You ship personally. This is not a role for someone who wants a team of ten doing the building. Co-creation, not solo genius. Stakeholders across the firm (investment, platform, marketing, operations, etc.) steer, test, and tune what you build. Within a year, everyone at the firm should be able to point at something they had a hand in shaping. Product discipline. Prototype, validate with real users, kill what doesn't get adopted. Usage is the metric; expect and budget for churn. Scale deliberately. You start solo. As the foundation proves out, you'll orchestrate internal or external build resources and potentially grow the function. You are prepared to identify, leverage and lead exceptional talent to help achieve results. Who you are You've shipped a real data or AI product end to end (pipelines, retrieval, and the product surface) and people actually used it. Deep, hands-on command of data architecture, warehousing, and governance. Fluent with embeddings, retrieval, and agents that act, not just answer. You treat access control and provenance as product features, not compliance chores. Low ego, high agency, energized by a blank page. Excited to tackle the unglamorous work (entity resolution, data hygiene, permissions) that everything depends on. You can sit with an investor, an EA, and a founder in the same week and design for all of them. Venture experience isn't required, but you'll need to earn a front-line view of the work fast. You can say "no" and "not yet" to smart, senior people and make them glad you did. What this role is not Not IT operations: endpoint, device & office infrastructure are handled by our managed IT partner. Not reg compliance: policy & DORA workstreams are owned by legal, with your input on anything AI. Not a reporting function: you build systems that answer questions, not dashboards on request. Why this role You'll have a blank page, real budget influence, direct partnership access, and a firm small enough that what you build touches everyone within weeks. The firms that figure this out will compound differently from the ones that don't. This is the seat where that happens. Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role We're looking for a Senior Customer Success Manager to join our Customer Experience team at Pleo. In this role, you'll help our high-touch, Mid Market customers achieve success and maximise the value of Pleo’s solutions and be part of a dynamic and collaborative team as we scale our innovative expense management platform across the UK & Ireland If you're excited about solving customer challenges, and driving growth through exceptional service and are passionate about Customer Success in the SaaS industry, then this is the opportunity for you! Who you’ll be working with and reporting to You’ll report to our Director of CX and work closely with teams in CX, Onboarding, AM, Sales and Product. Our team of 30 is highly collaborative and dedicated to Customer Experience. What you’ll be doing As a Senior Customer Success Manager, your main markets will be UKI customers. You will: Nurture, support and process expansion for any opportunity from the customer base As a customer's trusted product advisor and business consultant advise them on how to create their ideal processes with the tool to optimise their value-add Own the adoption journey of your customer portfolio (after the onboarding phase) Collaborate across teams with different internal stakeholders such as product management, services & solutions, marketing, customer support, etc. to improve the entire customer experience Receive, qualify and triage all inbound communication from all communication channels; email, Intercom (web chat), and/or other performance marketing channels Cultivate key customers to become advocates of Pleo and the Fintech community Manage day-to-day operations and long-term business relationships with our customers Do everything in your power to prevent customers from leaving Pleo through measuring health scores, and product/feature adoption and acting proactively on those Optimise the product-market-fit by building the bridge between the customer's feedback and our product team What you bring You’ll thrive in this role if: You have 7+ years of prior experience in account management or sales or customer success roles You have an open mindset that always looks for the positive. Your customers and colleagues find your energy contagious You truly enjoy helping others move and improve. You love helping your customers scale and grow You love goals and objectives. You don't always need to be given tasks – you create your own tasks while chasing your targets, and it motivates you to reach them You love a fast-paced and dynamic environment, where you have different kinds of tasks - from customer calls to meetings with our product team This is a high volume, high velocity role. Being able to think and do things at scale is a huge plus You are a trustworthy person who always ensures that deadlines are reached, promises are kept, and you do what is expected of you You are empathetic. You have a strong ability to feel how others are doing. You are also able to communicate in a very empathetic way and touch people's emotions You are fluent in English Why is this role a good fit for you This role is a good fit for you if: You enjoy building long-term relationships with high-touch, Mid Market customers and taking ownership of their success from adoption through expansion. You thrive in a fast-paced, high-volume environment and feel energised by balancing customer conversations, internal collaboration, and proactive problem-solving. You’re motivated by impact and outcomes — helping customers grow, spotting expansion opportunities, and turning feedback into meaningful product improvements excites you. This role is not a good fit for you if: You’re not motivated by customer-facing work or influencing customer outcomes through proactive engagement and collaboration. You’re uncomfortable with project management or coordinating multiple initiatives at the same time. You’re not motivated by upselling, cross-selling, or optimising the long-term value of your customers’ accounts. How you’ll develop in this role In your first 6 months at Pleo, you’ll: Lead customer adoption projects to drive impact in helping high-touch, Mid Market clients maximise the value of Pleo’s solutions. Collaborate with Customer Success and Product teams to improve customer experience processes and feedback loops. Grow your skills in relationship management and upselling strategies, taking on new challenges as the company continues to scale. We’re committed to helping you develop your career, whether that means taking on bigger projects, stepping into leadership, or acquiring new skills in customer success. The location London, UK Show me the benefits Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days - enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office Comprehensive private healthcare - depending on your location, coverage options include Vitality, Alan or Médis We offer 25 days of holiday + your public holidays For our Team, we offer both hybrid and fully remote working options Option to purchase 5 additional days of holiday through a salary sacrifice We use MyndUp to give our employees access to free mental health and well-being support with great success so far Paid parental leave - we want to make sure that we're supportive of families and help you feel that you don't have to compromise your family due to work The interview process We want to ensure you are set-up for success and understand what will be expected of you. If your application is successful, our interview process is as follows: Intro call: A 30-minute chat with our Talent Partner to discuss the role and your background. A 30-45 minute call with the Hiring Manager Our Pleo Challenge - an opportunity for you to showcase your ability in the form of a presentation and how you would approach the task at hand Final Interview - Our Bar Raiser meeting - how would you raise the bar for us? Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired a CSM, we received many applications but only a few were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: we receive a lot of CVs, and many of them are AI-generated. We love seeing people leverage AI—it’s a big focus for us internally too—but without human intervention, these CVs can sometimes become generic and fail to show a candidate in the best light. What we're really looking for is the specific details of real impact that only you know from your previous experience. A top tip from us is to use the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit: Laszlo Bock, ~2014) to give a really clear picture of what you’ve worked on. A final note: including links to your previous companies' websites is a huge help and allows us to truly understand your background! Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. Profile to role fit: highlight most important aspects of the role, points that might get misunderstood, any specific industry requirements etc. About your application English first. title: Analytics Engineer
description: About Pleo Messy spend management is tricky business. And tedious processes are a lose-lose situation for all involved, not just finance. At Pleo, we're changing that. We build spend solutions that make managing money seamless, empowering, and surprisingly effective for finance teams and employees alike - with a vision to help all businesses ‘go beyond’. The word ‘Pleo’ actually means ‘more than you’d expect’, and living by that mantra has been the secret to our success over the last 10 years. Now, we’re at a pivotal moment in our journey; every move we make has a direct impact on our 40,000+ customers, our business, and our collective success. We need people who take pride in uncovering customer needs, who turn complex problems into simple solutions, challenge the way things are done (respectfully), and always aim high. With great ambitions driving us forward, we can’t say we’ve got this whole thing figured out. And frankly, that’s half the fun! What we can say is that we’re a driven, progressive, and, importantly, a kind bunch of 850+ people from over 100 nationalities, all committed to delivering the future of business spending, together. About the role Pleo's Intelligence function covers the full analytical picture - product behaviour, GTM performance, commercial data science, financial reporting, and operational intelligence. The Analytics Engineers who serve these teams own the data modelling layer that all of it runs on: dbt models, metric definitions, and semantic layer contributions that analysts, product teams, and AI tools depend on to get consistent, trustworthy answers. You'll be embedded in the Product Intelligence team, building the tracking, experimentation, and data modelling foundations that make product data trustworthy and self-serve. You'll join a close-knit team actively migrating our analytics stack onto a new Analytics Warehouse and Omni, moving off legacy tools like Looker and Hippocampus. If you want to build the infrastructure that other people's product decisions run on rather than just report on what exists, this is the opportunity for you. Who you'll work with and reporting to You will report to an Analytics Manager leading Product Intelligence and Growth Intelligence. You'll partner closely with Product Managers, Product Analysts, and Engineering to get tracking, experimentation, and metric definitions right from the ground up. You'll also engage with the broader Analytics Engineering community across Pleo to drive shared standards, especially around the semantic layer that keeps metrics consistent across the organization. What you'll be doing Build and maintain dbt models in our new Analytics Warehouse, using a clean, layered architecture and migrating logic off legacy tools as you go. Own tracking plan implementation and QA directly in Segment and Amplitude in close partnership with Product and Engineering. Support experimentation by modelling assignment and outcome data into structured formats that analysts and PMs can query directly. Define and document metrics in our semantic layer, ensuring a single authoritative definition so downstream BI tools and AI applications yield consistent answers. Apply AI-augmented data modelling practices as a standard part of how you write, review, and migrate code. Partner with Product Managers and Analysts to turn one-off questions into durable, reusable data models. Maintain data quality in your domain through dbt tests, freshness SLAs, and proactive monitoring. What you bring Solid SQL and dbt experience, with a clear comfort owning models end to end. Working knowledge of event-based tracking tools like Segment or Amplitude. Experience with Git-based development workflows, including opening and reviewing pull requests. Clear communication skills to explain data definitions and structures to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Genuine day-to-day use of AI tooling as part of your standard coding and workflow routine. Comfort navigating ambiguity and untangling legacy logic to build modern foundations. This role is NOT a good fit if You only want to write dashboards without touching or owning the underlying data models. You require rigid processes and heavy upfront structure before taking initiative. You prefer to avoid data migration, cleanup work, and legacy system refactoring. Your first 6 months Ramp up: Master our dbt project structure, tracking plans, and migration roadmap while shipping small, reviewed code changes early on. Take ownership: Own a dedicated slice of the migration, such as an event domain or our core experimentation data models. Drive consistency: Establish semantic layer definitions for your domain so analysts and PMs can self-serve accurate metrics without custom workarounds. Our tech stack context Data warehouse: GCP / BigQuery (new Analytics Warehouse) Transformation: dbt Orchestration: Airflow Tracking and Oroduct Analytics: Segment, Amplitude BI and Analytics: Omni (migrating off legacy Looker and Hippocampus) Languages: SQL Show me the benefits! Your own Pleo card (no more out-of-pocket spending!) Lunch is on us for your work days—enjoy catered meals or receive a lunch allowance based on your local office. Comprehensive private healthcare depending on your location (coverage options include Vitality, Alan, or Médis). 25 days of annual holiday plus public holidays, with the option to purchase 5 additional days through salary sacrifice. Flexible working options supporting both hybrid and fully remote setups. Free mental health and well-being support through MyndUp. Generous paid parental leave policies to support growing families. The interview process Intro Call: 30 minutes with our Talent Partner SQL Test: Completed via CoderPad Hiring Manager Interview: 45 minutes with our Data & Analytics Manager Team Interview & Live Case: Data modelling case via CodeSignal Final Interview: 30 minutes with our VP of Data & AI Transparency is important to us so we also wanted to share some insights about what we’re looking for in applications to ensure you can set yourself up for success! Last time we hired an Analytics Engineer, we received a total of 173 applications but only 10 were selected for an intro call. Some of the key reasons why previous candidates didn’t make it past the application screening stage include: CV writing and content: it was very clear that many of the CVs we saw were very generic and AI generated. There is no issue with leveraging AI to help with CV writing, there was little indication of what real impact the candidates had in their previous experience. You might have heard of the “Achieved X, as measured by Y, by doing Z” formula (credit Laszlo Bock ~2014), this is a great way to give a clear picture of what you have actually worked on. Some link or quick description of the companies you’ve worked with is also a great help. Application care: every single application we receive is reviewed by a human (yes, hundreds of them) because we believe that candidates' efforts should be matched by an equal level of human care. This means that we expect a similar level of attention put into your application. Read and answer the application questions carefully, they make a huge difference in our decision-making process. Profile to role fit: there was misunderstanding about the type of experience we expect from an Analytics Engineer and we received many applications from candidates who had never been exposed to a product-led environment or had been exclusively focused on SQL/dbt work when we’re looking for both technical and stakeholders management and team collaboration experience. To be perfectly clear, this is NOT a Data Engineer role or a Data Analyst role! This is a heavily-driven dbt modelling role, experience in this area is critical. We’ve taken great care in writing this role description to reflect the reality of the job as best as possible, please ensure you read it carefully and highlight on your CV the experience relevant to what we are looking for.
